title: A hill estate
body: An estate on the hill slopes of a tropical island covers several hundred hectares and grows only tea. It was set up in colonial times by a European company and is now owned by a national corporation. The company has invested heavily in nurseries, processing machinery and a factory on the estate. Trained managers and agricultural scientists supervise pruning, fertiliser use and plucking schedules. A large number of workers are employed at low wages to pluck the leaves. A good road and rail link carries the processed tea from the estate factory to the port, from where most of it is exported.
